## Description

Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track D (design rules and UI component setup), wave D2. No audit backlog id. Created from the audit's rulings and blueprint, not from a backlog line (see Findings).

Persona and route: /consult/:id and sub-pages, prescription, orders, reconciliation, sign, merge approval, /settings, full registration, schedule editing, /nurse/:id · under 768 px.
Findings and reviewers: F-11, F-12 (phone) · reviewers C-10, B-04, B-06 · arbitration ruling 5. No UX number of its own in the backlog: found while mapping the rulings to tickets.
Rationale: At 375 px the prescription table scrolls sideways inside itself and hides dose columns; the consultation is 4,941 px tall. A phone is for looking and for small urgent acts; a prescription is neither.
Proposed UX behaviour: Under 768 px a doctor gets My day, the queue, a read-only chart (allergy first), search, signing an addendum and seeing an escalation. Composing or authorising a prescription, reconciliation, placing orders, signing a new note, merge approval and settings show one message in place of the write control: Open this on a tablet or computer, with the patient's name where a patient is open. Reception gets the queue list and quick registration; full registration and schedule editing show the same message. Nurse vitals entry shows it too until the strip is pinned and one group shows per screen. The content stays readable; nothing is hidden behind Page not found or a clipped layout. This is a usability rule in the client, not a security control: the server's authorisation is unchanged.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/08-design-system-blueprint.md section 11 (device table); docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/screenshots/doctor-375.png.
Components and tokens affected: PageMessage or Banner with the message. The wide and 768 breakpoints.
Front end and back end split: Front end only.
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the page components ticket and the refused-screen ticket (same message component, different words).
Clinical sign-off: Required before merge: question 19 of the validation plan (would you ever prescribe or sign from a phone?), recorded on the issue. If the answer is yes, this ticket is re-scoped before any code.
Effort and regression risk: M · Low to medium: a doctor who used the phone at home loses writing there.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) A phone layout for prescribing. (2) The native apps. (3) Any server-side block by device.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Given a doctor at 375 px on an open consultation, when the prescription, orders, reconciliation or Review and sign is reached, then each shows Open this on a tablet or computer with the patient's name and no write control
- [ ] **AC2.** Given the same phone, when My day, the queue, the chart and an escalation are opened, then each is readable with the allergy first and no sideways scrolling
- [ ] **AC3.** Given a signed note at 375 px, when the doctor adds an addendum, then it can be written and signed
- [ ] **AC4.** Given 768 px and wider, when the same screens open, then every write control is present
- [ ] **AC5.** Given the API, when a write is sent from any device by an authorised user, then the server's answer is the same as before this change
- [ ] **AC6.** Given English and Arabic at 375 px, when axe runs, then there is no violation
